title: Zheng He treasure voyages
summary: From 1405 to 1433 the Ming admiral Zheng He led seven fleet voyages from China through Southeast Asia to India and, on later voyages, to Hormuz and the East African coast. Sources count the large fleets at roughly 200 to 317 ships and 27,500 to 30,000 men. An edict ended the voyages in 1424, though a seventh went out in 1431.

uncertainty.note: The Collector dates the first departure to 11 July 1405. Voyage spans differ slightly between sources: first voyage 1405-1407 (Collector) or 1405-1406 (Asia Society); fourth voyage 1413-1415 or 1414-15.

beats.caption: The first fleet sailed on 11 July 1405; sources count the large fleets at roughly 200 to 317 ships.
On the third voyage the Chinese recognised Paramesawara as Malacca's ruler and declared it a Chinese vassal.
By the fifth voyage (1417-1419) the fleet reached Hormuz, Aden and East African ports including Mogadishu and Mombasa.

reviewer_note: Least sure of ship and crew figures: The Collector and Asia Society give 317 ships and almost 28,000 men for 1405, Asia Society 300 ships and about 27,500 men for 1431, and the Tennessee module says larger fleets had at least 200-300 ships and 28,000-30,000 men. The sources disagree on when Malacca was first called at (first vs third voyage). Waypoint dates are voyage spans, not port arrival dates, which none of the opened pages gives.
